questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Which situation would most clearly violate the principle of separation of powers in a presidential constitution?
options: The President appoints ministers subject to confirmation by the Senate.
The legislature approves the annual budget and questions ministers about spending.
A single body makes a law, enforces it and also tries persons accused of breaking it.
The judiciary interprets statutes and decides cases brought before it.
questions.explanation: Separation of powers is violated when the same organ performs legislative, executive and judicial functions without restraint. Legislative oversight, judicial interpretation and executive appointments with Senate confirmation are normal checks rather than a fusion of all powers.

questions.q: In the process of amending a constitution, a referendum is used mainly to
options: obtain the direct approval of the proposed amendment from the electorate
resolve disputes between the President and the National Assembly
select delegates to a constitutional conference
draft the amendment through a committee of the legislature
questions.explanation: A referendum submits a specific proposal to the electorate for acceptance or rejection, so it gives direct popular approval for a constitutional amendment. It is not the body that drafts amendments, settles constitutional disputes or chooses conference delegates.

questions.q: A government that respects the limits placed on its powers by a constitution and governs according to established rules is practising
questions.explanation: Constitutionalism means that governmental power is limited by constitutional rules and exercised according to law. Federalism concerns the division of power between central and regional governments, while republicanism concerns the nature of the head of state and the source of authority.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the President appoints the Chief Justice of Nigeria on the recommendation of the
questions.explanation: The National Judicial Council recommends candidates for the office of Chief Justice of Nigeria, after which the President appoints and the Senate confirms. The Federal Judicial Service Commission handles a different set of judicial appointments, and the Council of State and Nigerian Bar Association do not make this constitutional recommendation.

questions.q: In a ward election in Nasarawa State, four candidates scored as follows: Amina 12,400; Bello 9,800; Chika 7,600; Danjuma 4,200. Total valid votes were 34,000. Under the first-past-the-post system, the winner is
options: Amina, because she obtained more than half of the valid votes
Bello, because he came second and would contest a run-off with Amina
Amina, because she obtained the highest number of votes
no candidate, because no one obtained an absolute majority
questions.explanation: First-past-the-post elects the candidate with the highest number of votes, whether or not that number is an absolute majority. Amina scored 12,400 of 34,000 votes, which is below the 17,000 halfway mark, yet she is still the winner under this system.

questions.q: A plebiscite is best described as a vote organised to
options: obtain the electorate's direct opinion on a particular public issue
confirm the appointment of senior judges
elect members of a legislature for a constituency
select candidates to represent political parties at a general election
questions.explanation: A plebiscite allows the electorate to express a direct decision or opinion on a specific issue rather than choose representatives. It is not a constituency election, a party primary or a procedure for confirming judicial appointments.

questions.q: The power of the National Assembly to make laws that bind all residents within Nigeria is an aspect of
questions.explanation: Internal sovereignty is the final authority of the state to make and enforce laws within its territory. External sovereignty concerns independence from control by other states.

questions.q: A foreign engineer who has lived in Nigeria for the period required by law and is granted a certificate after satisfying the constitutional conditions has acquired Nigerian citizenship by
questions.explanation: Naturalisation is the acquisition of citizenship by a foreigner who fulfils the conditions prescribed by law. Citizenship by birth or descent is acquired at birth, while registration applies to certain persons with defined ties to Nigeria.

questions.q: The Nasarawa State House of Assembly organises a public hearing on a bill to regulate commercial motorcycle operations. The main purpose of the hearing is to
options: settle disputes between two traditional rulers
obtain the views of the public on the proposed law
approve the promotion of civil servants
select candidates for the ruling party
questions.explanation: A public hearing allows citizens and stakeholders to express their views on a proposed law, helping lawmakers gauge public opinion. It is not a forum for selecting party candidates, settling traditional disputes, or approving civil-service promotions.

questions.q: The main reason for including fundamental rights in the Nigerian Constitution is to
options: allow the president to legislate without the National Assembly
protect citizens against arbitrary exercise of state power
questions.explanation: Fundamental rights safeguard individual liberties against unlawful or arbitrary action by the state. They do not guarantee employment or confer citizenship on all residents, nor do they permit the president to legislate without the legislature.

questions.q: At the federal level, laws made by Nigerian military governments were generally known as
questions.explanation: Federal military governments in Nigeria ruled largely by decrees, which had the force of law. Edicts were generally used by state military administrations, while bills are proposed laws in a legislature.

questions.q: The creation of twelve states in Nigeria in 1967 was carried out by the administration of
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon's administration created twelve states in Nigeria in 1967. Later military administrations, including those of Murtala Muhammed and Ibrahim Babangida, created additional states.

questions.q: The electoral commission registers several parties, but only two parties consistently win national elections and form government. This party system is best described as
questions.explanation: A two-party system exists where two major parties dominate electoral competition and government formation, even if other parties are legally registered. A multi-party system requires several parties to have a realistic chance of winning power.

questions.q: One important democratic role of pressure groups is that they
options: provide a channel through which citizens can influence government policy between elections
replace the judiciary in interpreting the constitution
make laws for the state without the legislature
conduct elections on behalf of the electoral commission
questions.explanation: Pressure groups articulate the interests of their members and use various methods to influence government decisions between elections. They do not conduct elections, interpret the constitution, or make laws.

questions.q: A political system in which a small group of privileged persons controls the government and uses state institutions to protect their own interests is best called
questions.explanation: Oligarchy is government by a small, often privileged group. Monarchy is rule by a monarch, democracy gives political power to the people, and theocracy is rule by religious authority.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A state governor directs the attorney-general to instruct a High Court judge to postpone a case involving the governor's political associate until after an election. This action most directly undermines
questions.explanation: Instructions from the executive to a judge on how to handle a pending case amount to interference with judicial independence. Federal character concerns equitable representation, collective responsibility concerns cabinet solidarity, and legislative oversight concerns supervision of the executive.

questions.q: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria principally provides for
options: citizenship and the acquisition of Nigerian citizenship.
the fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy.
the procedure for the impeachment of the President.
questions.explanation: Chapter IV contains the fundamental rights provisions, including rights to life, dignity, fair hearing and freedom of expression. The directive principles are in Chapter II, while citizenship is dealt with in Chapter III.

questions.q: A major advantage of a written constitution over an unwritten one is that it
options: is always interpreted by the executive rather than the courts.
removes the need for conventions and judicial decisions.
can never be amended by any procedure.
makes the basic rules of government clearer and more certain.
questions.explanation: A written constitution assembles and codifies the main rules of government, making them easier to identify and apply. It can still be amended, interpreted by courts and supplemented by conventions; it does not eliminate those processes.

questions.q: A bill introduced in the Nigerian National Assembly by a senator acting in a personal capacity rather than on behalf of the government is known as
questions.explanation: A private member's bill is sponsored by an individual legislator, not by the executive. A private bill concerns a particular person or group, an appropriation bill authorizes government spending, and a constitution amendment bill seeks to alter the constitution.

questions.q: The requirement in the 1999 Constitution that the President appoint at least one minister from each state of the federation is principally intended to promote
questions.explanation: The requirement is designed to reflect Nigeria's federal structure and ensure that appointments are spread across the states. Separation of powers concerns the distribution of functions among organs, collective responsibility concerns cabinet unity, and judicial review concerns court supervision of constitutionality.

questions.q: In a constituency election in Kaduna State, candidate Amina secured 42% of the valid votes while candidate Musa secured 38% and the rest went to other candidates. If Amina was declared winner without a run-off, which principle best explains the outcome?
options: Seats are allocated according to each party's share of the total votes cast
A second election must be held whenever no candidate obtains two-thirds of the votes
A candidate must obtain more than half of the valid votes before being declared winner
The candidate with the highest number of votes wins even without an absolute majority
questions.explanation: Under the plurality or first-past-the-post system, the candidate who polls the highest number of valid votes is declared elected even if that number is below 50 per cent. Amina's 42 per cent was higher than Musa's 38 per cent, so a run-off is not required by that system. The rule requiring more than half belongs to an absolute-majority system, not the plurality principle described.

questions.q: A ward in Lagos State has 250,000 registered voters and elects one councillor, while another ward in a rural area of the same state has 70,000 registered voters and also elects one councillor. The arrangement most clearly violates the electoral principle of
options: the neutrality of the returning officer
equality of votes, often expressed as one person, one vote
questions.explanation: Equal constituency populations matter because each vote should carry roughly the same weight in electing one representative. A huge difference in registered voters between wards that each elect one councillor undermines one person, one vote. The secrecy of the ballot and universal adult suffrage concern how voting is conducted and who may vote, not the equal value of votes across constituencies.

questions.q: INEC carries out a continuous voter registration exercise before a general election mainly to
options: determine the winner of the election before polling
screen candidates nominated by political parties
delimit constituencies for the National Assembly
update the register of voters so that qualified persons are included and ineligible entries removed
questions.explanation: Continuous voter registration is meant to keep the voters' register current by registering newly qualified voters and correcting or removing invalid entries. It does not decide election results, redraw constituency boundaries or screen party candidates, which are handled through separate processes.

questions.q: Which principal organ of the United Nations recommends the admission of a new member state for approval by the General Assembly?
questions.explanation: Under the UN Charter, admission of a new member is decided by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council. The Secretariat carries out administrative work, ECOSOC deals mainly with economic and social matters, and the ICJ settles legal disputes.

questions.q: The Authority of Heads of State and Government of ECOWAS is mainly responsible for
options: taking major policy decisions for the community
interpreting the ECOWAS Treaty in ordinary cases
hearing appeals from the ECOWAS Court of Justice
supervising the daily administration of the ECOWAS Commission
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Authority is the highest policy-making organ and gives direction to the community, including decisions on regional peace and integration. Judicial interpretation belongs to the ECOWAS Court of Justice, while routine administration is handled by the Commission and its officials.

questions.q: The Federal Government of Nigeria decided to host a summit of the Economic Community of West African States in Abuja and provided ₦2.5 billion for logistics. This action most directly illustrates Nigeria's foreign policy role of
options: pursuing military alliance with a distant superpower
promoting regional integration and leadership in West Africa
protecting Nigerian citizens living in Europe
questions.explanation: Hosting an ECOWAS summit supports regional cooperation and shows Nigeria's leadership in West African integration. It is not evidence of a military alliance with a superpower, consular protection in Europe, or withdrawal from international bodies.

questions.q: The primary purpose of the Federal Character Commission in Nigeria is to
options: review the revenue-sharing formula among the three tiers of government
delimit constituencies for federal and state elections
promote equitable distribution of public posts and socio-economic amenities among the federating units
conduct elections into local government councils
questions.explanation: The Federal Character Commission checks the application of the federal character principle so that no section of the country is unfairly excluded from public appointments and amenities. Revenue formula review is handled through statutory revenue bodies such as the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission, while elections and constituency delimitation are the work of electoral bodies.

questions.q: One major effect of the 1963 Republican Constitution on Nigeria’s legal system was that
options: the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council became the final court for Nigerian cases
the Supreme Court of Nigeria became the highest court of appeal
Sharia courts were abolished throughout the federation
appeals from Nigerian courts went directly to the Queen in Council
questions.explanation: With the 1963 Republican Constitution, Nigeria removed appeals to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council and made the Supreme Court the final appellate court. Sharia courts were not abolished by that Constitution, and the Queen ceased to be Nigeria’s Head of State.

questions.q: A principal in a Lagos secondary school issues a circular that classes will close early for a public holiday, and the teachers comply because they accept the office’s right to give such directives. This best illustrates
questions.explanation: Authority is the accepted right to give orders and expect obedience, which here belongs to the principal’s office. Coercive power would rely on force or threats, while legitimacy concerns acceptance of a government’s right to rule and sovereignty is the supreme power of a state.

questions.q: A political party in Ogun State asks market leaders to support its candidate, and traders who refuse are denied access to market stalls. The ability of the party to secure compliance by threatening the traders’ livelihood, even though they do not accept its right to command them, best illustrates
questions.explanation: Power is the ability to influence or compel others, even without their acceptance of a right to command, as shown by the threat to deny access to stalls. Authority would require accepted right, legitimacy would require acceptance of the right to rule, and sovereignty is the supreme legal power of a state.

questions.q: A state law conflicts with a federal law on a matter in the Exclusive Legislative List, and the federal law prevails. This situation best illustrates that
options: component units in a federation exercise powers granted by the constitution and are not fully sovereign
sovereignty in a federation belongs exclusively to the states
local governments are superior to both federal and state governments
questions.explanation: In a federation, states exercise constitutional powers but are not fully sovereign; on exclusive federal matters, federal law prevails. External sovereignty belongs to the federation as a state, not to its component units.

questions.q: A respected professor in Kano frequently comments on national issues on radio and television, and many residents form their political views from his statements. In the study of public opinion, the professor is best described as
questions.explanation: An opinion leader is a person whose views are respected and can influence the attitudes of others on public issues. A pollster measures opinion, a returning officer conducts elections, and a government spokesperson officially represents the government rather than independently shaping opinion in this sense.

questions.q: The 1979 general elections in Nigeria were conducted as part of the transition programme of the military government led by
questions.explanation: The Obasanjo military government organised the 1979 elections and handed over to the civilian government of Shehu Shagari. Murtala Muhammed had announced a transition programme before his death, but the 1979 elections took place under Obasanjo.

questions.q: The Political Bureau set up by the Ibrahim Babangida administration in 1986 was primarily intended to
options: try former public officers for corruption
gather Nigerians’ views and recommend a suitable political system for the country
delineate new states and local government areas
questions.explanation: The Political Bureau was established to canvass public views and advise the government on Nigeria’s political future and transition programme. Census taking, trial of public officers, and boundary creation were handled through other institutions and arrangements.

questions.q: After the sudden removal of fuel subsidy, a group of traders in Ibadan gathered spontaneously to protest government policy without formal leaders or permanent organization. Such a group is best described as
questions.explanation: An anomic pressure group arises spontaneously and is loosely organized, often around a sudden grievance, as in the Ibadan traders' protest. Institutional groups operate within government institutions, associational groups are formally organized, and promotional groups are organized to advance particular causes or values.

questions.q: In a parliamentary system of government, the head of state usually
options: is elected directly by the people and serves a fixed term as chief executive
performs mainly ceremonial functions while the prime minister heads the government
controls the armed forces directly and appoints ministers who are responsible only to him
initiates all bills in the legislature and presides over cabinet meetings
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the head of state generally symbolizes national unity and performs ceremonial duties, while the prime minister and cabinet exercise executive power and answer to parliament. Direct control of the armed forces and responsibility of ministers to a single chief executive are features more associated with a presidential system.

questions.q: Alhaji Bello, a businessman in Kano, challenges a directive by the Minister of Finance before the Federal High Court. The court finds that the directive conflicts with an Act of the National Assembly and declares it invalid. This judicial action is an example of
questions.explanation: The court is examining the legality and constitutionality of an executive act and invalidating it for inconsistency with a statute, which is judicial review. Delegated legislation is law-making by bodies such as ministers, while executive clemency concerns pardon or leniency.

questions.q: In a constituency election in Ibadan, Musa receives 8,500 votes, Ngozi receives 7,900 votes, and the other candidates share 4,200 votes. Musa is declared elected immediately because he has the highest number of votes, although he does not have more than half of all the votes cast. This arrangement illustrates
questions.explanation: The candidate with the highest number of votes is declared elected in a first-past-the-post arrangement even without an absolute majority. A run-off would require a second election when no candidate meets the required majority, while proportional representation and single transferable vote allocate seats through different mechanisms.

questions.q: The treaty that revised the original ECOWAS Treaty and currently provides the legal framework for the organisation was signed in
questions.explanation: The Revised ECOWAS Treaty was signed in Cotonou, Benin, in 1993 and now provides the organisation’s legal framework. The original 1975 treaty was signed in Lagos, while Abuja is the headquarters of ECOWAS.

questions.q: A political party performs the function of political recruitment when it
options: selects and presents candidates to contest elections
monitors elections and announces the results
explains its policies to the electorate during campaigns
combines various interests into a common policy programme
questions.explanation: Political recruitment refers to the process by which a party selects people to stand as its candidates for public office. Explaining policies to voters is political education, while combining interests is interest aggregation. Election monitoring and result announcement are functions of the electoral commission rather than a party's recruitment role.
